rationale:
The subject has three obligations. I found a test for each in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs`.

1. **An outline language can supply structural search, returning matched byte ranges within the supplied source.** `bundled_structural_search_returns_matches_and_rejects_bad_rules_and_source` runs `languages::Rust.search_structure` on a two-function source with the rule `{"rule":{"kind":"function_item"}}`. It asserts that the returned spans, used to slice the supplied source, give exactly `fn first() {}` and `fn second() {}`. That checks both the byte ranges and that they fall within the supplied source. The test also checks that a malformed rule and an unparseable source return errors. The requirement doesn't state those errors, so they are extra coverage.

2. **The default implementation returns an unsupported-language error.** `outline_only_languages_report_unsupported_structural_search` calls `search_structure` on `CustomLanguage`, which provides outlining only. It asserts the call returns an error whose message contains "unsupported". The trait default in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs#trait[OutlineLang]/fn[search_structure]` returns `unsupported_search(self.name())`.

3. **Plain text supplies outlining only.** The same test asserts that `languages::PlainText.search_structure` returns an error whose message contains "plain-text". `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` also checks that `PlainText` has the name `plain-text` and no extensions.

The other bundled languages use the same `language` macro in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/languages/mod.rs`. Testing the override through Rust is therefore enough, because the text draws no per-language distinction. `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` does not need a structural-search reference to this subject. Both tests carry a {test} marker for this requirement. I found no uncovered obligation and no marking gap.
